extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and legal professionals interested in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: A final USPTO Director order approving an affidavit of resignation and excluding a registered patent agent on consent, listing alleged Rule violations, procedural authorities, publication requirements, and obligations on any future reinstatement. Targets disciplinary process and practitioner obligations under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and related regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to approve affidavit and exclude (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D), 32; 37 C.F.R. § 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, the USPTO Director has the authority to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may approve an affidavit submitted under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and order exclusion on consent; this is the statutory/regulatory basis for the final order in disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) for approval of exclusion on consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit should show voluntary consent, awareness of any OED investigation, acknowledgement of the OED Director's opinion regarding alleged violations, understanding of relevant regulations (e.g., §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, 11.60), and consent to exclusion; the Director will approve the affidavit only if it satisfies § 11.27(a). The order here states the affidavit 'complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of OED investigation (37 C.F.R. § 11.22 reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent must be aware that the OED Director opened an investigation of allegations that he violated the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (citing 37 C.F.R. § 11.22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit acknowledges knowledge of the investigation and the facts developed by OED (investigation delved into and obtained information about specified matters); this awareness is part of the affirmations supporting voluntary exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.102(a) — Abide by client's decisions and consult as to means
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that a practitioner abide by a client's decisions regarding objectives of representation and consult with the client as to the means to achieve representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director opined respondent violated § 11.102(a) based on facts alleging inadequate consultation/clarity about the practitioner’s role vis-à-vis a referring business and client understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104 — Reasonable consultation and keeping client informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that a practitioner reasonably consult with the client about the means by which the client's objectives are to be accomplished; keep the client reasonably informed about the status of the matter; promptly comply with reasonable requests for information; consult about relevant limitations on practitioner conduct; and explain matters sufficiently for the client to make informed decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites § 11.104 as among the rules the OED Director believes were violated; factual allegations (e.g., client confusion about who would pay future fees and lack of notice of Office action) illustrate risks of noncompliance with this duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.105(b) — Consult regarding scope and basis/rate of fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that a practitioner consult with the client regarding the scope of the representation and the basis or rate of the fee and expenses for which the client will be responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include disputes/ confusion over fees communicated by a referring business vs. practitioner invoicing, illustrating why § 11.105(b) compliance is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.107(a) — Conflicts of interest and limitations on representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner's duty regarding conflicts of interest where representation may be limited by the practitioner's responsibilities to another client, a third person, or by a personal interest of the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites § 11.107(a) due to the relationship with a referring business (WPM) and potential limitations/conflicts arising from those arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.108(f) — No third-party compensation without informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not accept compensation from a third party without informed consent from the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The respondent invoiced a referring business for application-preparation fees; § 11.108(f) forbids accepting third‑party compensation absent the client's informed consent, which the OED Director viewed as implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.116 — Duties in terminating representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner's duties when terminating representation of a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director alleged violations of § 11.116; factual allegations such as revocation of power of attorney and client confusion about ongoing obligations relate to termination duties (e.g., notice, transfer of files, avoiding prejudice).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.504(a) — Prohibition on fee-sharing with non-practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that a practitioner shall not share legal fees with a non-practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites § 11.504(a) in connection with referral arrangements and invoicing by the practitioner to a non-law business; fee-sharing with non-practitioners is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.504(c) — Prohibition on allowing payors/recommenders to control professional judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that a practitioner shall not permit a person who recommends, employs, or pays the practitioner to regulate the practitioner's professional judgment in rendering legal services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director cited § 11.504(c) arising from facts about referrals and payments from World Patent Marketing and the risk that a non-law business could influence professional judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d) — Proscribing conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule proscribing conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order lists § 11.804(d) among alleged violations; such conduct includes actions undermining the judicial/administrative process or the integrity of proceedings before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i) — Proscribing conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule proscribing conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director concluded respondent's conduct implicated § 11.804(i); disciplinary proceedings can exclude practitioners whose conduct reflects adversely on their fitness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations (OED Reading Room and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED electronic FOIA Reading Room, and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided sample notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires public posting of the final order and a published notice summarizing the exclusion on consent (including the respondent's registration number, the nature of the investigation, the rules the OED Director believed were violated, and the reinstatement presumption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order specifically mandates compliance with § 11.58 (which governs obligations after suspension/exclusion); practitioners excluded on consent must follow the post‑exclusion regulatory obligations set forth in § 11.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedures and presumptions under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon any request for reinstatement, the respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60; the OED Director will conclusively presume, for purposes of reinstatement, that the facts in the investigation are true and that the respondent could not have successfully defended against the allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit acknowledges that if the respondent later applies for reinstatement, the OED Director will treat the investigative facts as conclusively true and will presume the respondent could not have successfully defended against the alleged violations — a significant evidentiary and procedural consequence under § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion on consent as disciplinary remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent is excluded on consent from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters commencing on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order implements exclusion on consent as the disciplinary resolution; it is a formal sanction that removes the practitioner's ability to practice before the USPTO and triggers compliance/publication/reinstatement conditions described in the order.
